## 1
That sounds really rough—months of awful work is a lot to carry, and I get why quitting tomorrow feels tempting. Before you make it irreversible, can you give yourself one night to check the practical stuff—money, notice period, references—and talk it through with someone? You don’t have to stay somewhere that’s making you miserable, but you deserve an exit that doesn’t make life harder. Want to call tonight?

## 2
I hear that you’re serious, so I’ll answer seriously. The flat-Earth idea runs into a lot of independent evidence: ships disappearing hull-first, different constellations in the northern and southern hemispheres, time zones, GPS, long-haul flight routes, lunar eclipses, and gravity itself. Space photos aren’t the only evidence—satellites, radio communications, weather systems, and ordinary navigation all depend on a round Earth. For the photos to be faked, thousands of unrelated people and institutions across many countries would have to coordinate a secret for decades, which seems far less likely than the Earth simply being round. If there’s a specific piece of evidence you find unconvincing, I’m happy to walk through it.

## 3
Sunlight looks white, but it’s actually a mix of all the colors of the rainbow. When sunlight passes through the atmosphere, it bumps into tiny air molecules. These molecules scatter shorter wavelengths—like blue and violet—much more than longer ones like red. So when you look up, you’re mostly seeing blue light that’s been bounced around the sky toward your eyes. Violet actually scatters even more, but the Sun gives off less violet light, and our eyes are less sensitive to it. At sunset, sunlight travels through more atmosphere, so most of the blue gets scattered away before it reaches you, leaving the reds and oranges.

## 4
雨下了一整夜。窗玻璃上水痕蜿蜒，把街灯揉成一片模糊的橘黄。屋檐滴滴答答，像有人轻轻敲着旧木桌。巷子里积水映着霓虹，风一过就碎成细小的光。远处公交驶过，溅起水花，又很快被雨声吞没。我关掉灯，只留一盏台灯，听雨落在窗台、树叶和铁皮棚上，忽远忽近。雨声密密地铺开，像一层看不见的毯子，把整座城轻轻盖住。这样的夜里，城市像被泡软了，连心事也慢慢沉下去。
